lineupSource: Yahoo Sport UK / Roundtable projected XI, 20 August 2026, cross-checked on 21 August against Fantasy Football Scout's Friday predicted line-ups and Chelsea's own report of Xabi Alonso's 20 August press conference, re-checked on 22 August against Goal's 21 August preview, the Evening Standard / Yahoo Chelsea XI piece of 20 August, Sports Mole's 21 August injury and suspension list and The Pride of London's predicted XI, and re-checked again on 23 August against Rotowire's 22 August predicted line-ups, Sports Illustrated's 23 August Chelsea predicted XI, Football365's 23 August match preview and Sky Sports' 23 August team-news page. Still a projection, not team news — Sky confirmed on 23 August that no official sheet exists for either side, and none will until roughly an hour before Monday's 20:00 BST kickoff.
lineupNote: Still a projection, and Friday's crop of previews widened the spread rather than narrowing it. This 3-4-2-1 remains the modal call — Yahoo Sport and Roundtable both keep Reece James in a back three with Pedro Neto and Marco Palestra as the wing-backs — but Goal's 21 August preview keeps the same back three and reads the front as a 3-4-3 — João Pedro flanked by Palmer and Morgan Rogers rather than playing off a lone striker — with Romeo Lavia in the midfield two ahead of Enzo Fernández; the Evening Standard goes to a 4-3-3 with Jorrel Hato at left-back and James at right-back; and The Pride of London keeps James at right wing-back and promotes Josh Acheampong into the back three alongside Colwill and Lacroix. Four previews, four different answers on the back three, which with the left wing-back slot remains the least settled call here. Wesley Fofana is suspended, a ban carried over from his final-day red card at Sunderland that pre-season friendlies do not clear, and that is what pushes James from midfield into the back three. How long that ban runs is genuinely unclear: it has been reported as a single match, but the Sunderland dismissal was his second two-yellow red of 2025-26 after the one against Burnley, and at least one outlet has him banned for Alonso's first two games — Fulham and Brighton. No mainstream preview commits to a length, and none of it changes Monday: he is out at Craven Cottage either way. Enzo Fernández is staying — Alonso said flatly that Enzo is a Chelsea player once Manchester City let Chelsea's 14 August bid deadline pass — and is expected to feature. Palestra, the £43m signing from Atalanta and Serie A Defender of the Year after 37 loan appearances at Cagliari, can play either flank, so the left wing-back call still turns on whether Alonso wants his attacking edge there ahead of Hato or of Pep Chavarría, the £16.3m arrival from Rayo Vallecano signed to replace Marc Cucurella. The absence list hardened since Thursday: Goal now lists Caleb Wiley, Jordan Henderson, Aaron Anselmino, Mamadou Sarr, Emanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda as ruled out, though the Standard the same day still files Henderson (wrist) and Emegha (hamstring) as doubts rather than definite absentees. Alonso reported no fresh injury concerns and said Danny Welbeck, managed through a minor problem, returns to team training on Saturday and can be involved. The standing caveat is unchanged: James, Fernández, Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers all reported back late from the World Cup and are selectable but may be eased in, so any of the four could start on the bench.

lineupSource: Sports Mole's 26 August Chelsea v Luton Town EFL Cup preview, which supplies this exact 4-2-3-1 and is the only preview whose availability list matches Xabi Alonso's own Wednesday press conference. Cross-checked against Sports Illustrated's 26 August Chelsea predicted line-up and 101 Great Goals' preview, plus Chelsea's own match preview for kick-off and UK broadcast, the Sky Sports Carabao Cup 2026-27 fixture listing, and CBS Sports / Paramount+ for the US rights position. Still a projection, not team news — no official sheet exists until roughly an hour before Thursday's 19:30 BST kickoff.
lineupNote: A guess, and a lower-confidence one than usual: this is a rotation night, and rotation is the hardest thing to predict. Three previews produced three different shapes — Sports Mole a 4-2-3-1, Sports Illustrated a 3-4-2-1, 101 Great Goals a 4-3-3 — and only seven names appear in all three (Penders, Acheampong, Lacroix, Chavarría, Barco, Estêvão, Welbeck). Sports Mole's XI is used here because its availability list is the only one that squares with what Alonso actually said on Wednesday. Alonso has signalled wholesale changes, so first Chelsea starts are in play for Danny Welbeck, Valentín Barco, Pep Chavarría and goalkeeper Mike Penders, with Penders getting the kind of look that decides whether he pushes Robert Sánchez. Two source conflicts are worth stating plainly rather than smoothing over. First, Wesley Fofana: Sports Mole has him serving the second match of a two-game ban and therefore out tonight, while Sports Illustrated and 101 Great Goals both start him. The two-game reading is the better-supported one and is what this site has used for Sunday's Brighton page — a red-card ban runs across domestic competitions, so the opener plus this tie discharges it and he is clear for Brighton, not for Luton. He is left out here on that basis, but it is a genuine disagreement, not a settled fact. Second, 101 Great Goals starts Marco Palestra, which looks stale: Alonso ruled Palestra out on Wednesday alongside Moisés Caicedo, and was notably less hopeful about Palestra — “Both not for tomorrow. Hopefully Moi can make it for the weekend. Maybe we need to check a little bit more with Marco.” Cole Palmer is not injured; he is expected to be rested with Sunday in mind. Jordan Henderson (wrist) is out and targeting 6 September at Arsenal, Emanuel Emegha's status is reported inconsistently — Sports Mole has him fit and available, 101 Great Goals still lists a hamstring problem — and Aaron Anselmino (hamstring) is a doubt. Enzo Fernández is fit and expected to be involved in some capacity, though Manchester City interest and a 1 September window deadline make him the one selection Alonso may be managing for non-football reasons. Geovany Quenda's key stat is deliberately blank: he moved from Sporting CP this summer and the public 2025-26 numbers for him conflict badly across sources, so nothing is stated rather than guessed.
notes: Xabi Alonso's first competitive home match as Chelsea manager. Luton are a League One side managed by former Arsenal midfielder Jack Wilshere, and arrive having won the EFL Trophy last season. Alonso's Wednesday press conference ruled out Caicedo and Palestra for this tie. Expect heavy rotation. The third-round draw was made on Wednesday evening, before this tie is played: the winner goes away to Leeds United, in the weeks beginning 7 or 14 September.

Alonso's first home game in charge. The rescheduling question is settled: the Premier League's August-September fixture-amendment notice confirms this as Sunday 30 August, 14:00 BST, moved to accommodate Brighton's UEFA Conference League playoff tie the preceding Thursday. Chelsea also had an EFL Cup tie against Luton on Thursday 27 August, three days before this one, so rotation is a live factor. Brighton arrive short of forwards: Yankuba Minteh (leg) is out for several weeks, Evan Ferguson (ankle) is not expected back until late October or November, Stefanos Tzimas (knee) is targeted for early-to-mid October, and Kaoru Mitoma is still working back from summer hamstring surgery — Hürzeler says he is getting closer but he is not available here. Jack Hinshelwood picked up a training injury and Hürzeler called the weekend likely too soon for him. Georginio Rutter has been in a protective boot since the Aston Villa fixture and faces a late fitness test; he is the more likely of the two to feature but is now a genuine doubt rather than a probable. New signings Promise David and Jaouen Hadjam are expected to be options, and Pascal Struijk and Ferdi Kadioğlu are back in the squad. The practical read: Brighton are missing four of their forward options and may be without a fifth, so Chelsea's back three should face a less direct attacking threat than Brighton's league position suggests.

lineupNote: Seven changes, and the projection could not have caught the biggest one: Chelsea announced the signing of Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa for about £7.5m on Sunday morning and he went straight into goal. Robert Sánchez was left out of the squad entirely and Mike Penders dropped to the bench. Enzo Fernández was also omitted amid Manchester City interest. Alonso reverted to a back three after using 4-2-3-1 against Luton, with Fofana back from suspension alongside Lacroix and Colwill. Neto, Lavia and Hato all returned, Malo Gusto was pushed into midfield, and Reece James was rested. Substitutes: Penders, Acheampong, Chavarría, James, Barco, Caicedo, Estêvão, Gittens, Welbeck.

notes: Alonso's first competitive meeting with childhood friend Mikel Arteta as a fellow manager. Arsenal are the reigning champions. This is Chelsea's first match since the summer transfer window shut on Tuesday 1 September, and it closed with two departures that change the team. Enzo Fernandez has gone to Manchester City for GBP 125m on a five-year deal, a British-record-equalling fee and a reunion with Enzo Maresca; Chelsea booked roughly an GBP 18m profit on the fee they paid Benfica three and a half years ago. Chelsea had lined up Monaco's Lamine Camara as the replacement and that deal collapsed late on deadline day, so there is no direct like-for-like signing to slot in; Alonso's public line on Friday was that he is 'prepared and happy with the squad and the depth we have'. Goalkeeper Robert Sanchez also left, joining Cesc Fabregas's Como on a season-long loan, which leaves Emiliano Martinez and Mike Penders as the senior keepers. Marc Guiu moved to RB Leipzig. BOTH PRESS CONFERENCES HAVE NOW HAPPENED, at 1:30pm UK on Friday 4 September, and the picture they leave is meaningfully different from what this page said on Thursday night - in both directions. CHELSEA: Moises Caicedo is NOT ruled out. Alonso deliberately gave nothing away, saying only 'We will check tomorrow. Tomorrow is the last decision for the squad on Sunday', and when pressed added 'we need to not worry about these things that happen and we need to check tomorrow and take a final decision'. That is softer than Thursday's reporting, which had him very unlikely to feature. Treat him as a genuine Saturday call rather than an absentee. Jordan Henderson has been upgraded: after wrist surgery Alonso now says he is 'getting closer and closer to playing time', which is ahead of the mid-September return the injury trackers had projected. Alonso talked through the midfield options he does have, naming Valentin Barco ('young but he has come with great energy'), Henderson ('the composure, the mentality'), Reece James, Malo Gusto and academy midfielder Reggie Watson. On managing Romeo Lavia and James he said 'hopefully, touch wood, they don't have that many setbacks'. Emmanuel Emegha is back from the injury that cost him pre-season. Marco Palestra did not come up at all, so he stays an unknown. ARSENAL: their situation has improved, and the 'thin and unsettled' framing this page carried on Thursday no longer holds - be candid that it was overtaken within a day. Declan Rice is fit and available; he trained on Thursday and the knock he picked up against Aston Villa has cleared. Bruno Guimaraes, the GBP 75m arrival from Newcastle, missed Thursday's session but Arteta expects him back, saying he would 'probably tomorrow be OK to train', and he is expected to be involved. Cristhian Mosquera is the one genuine doubt left: he has not trained since a strain Arteta describes as precautionary and is due to test it on Saturday, with Ezri Konsa, a GBP 51m summer signing from Aston Villa, in line for his first competitive Arsenal start alongside Gabriel if Mosquera does not make it. Riccardo Calafiori is fit and was nominated for Premier League Player of the Month. Jurrien Timber is close, with Arteta saying he is 'in really good condition', but this is likely too soon after a groin problem and the bench is realistically his ceiling. William Saliba remains out with a back injury and is months rather than weeks away. MARKET: the line has drifted slightly Chelsea's way. DraftKings now price Chelsea +380, in from +425 on Thursday, with Arsenal -155 and the draw +260 both unmoved - so the move is real but small, and Arsenal are still a clear favourite at a de-vigged 56 percent. Chelsea then host Leeds United in the Carabao Cup third round on the Wednesday, three days after this, so squad management is again in play. FRIDAY EVENING UPDATE. Nothing official has changed since the morning - Caicedo is still a Saturday call and Mosquera still has a Saturday fitness test - but the day's previews sharpened three things. First, the Chelsea midfield projection on this page has moved: the consensus is now Reece James alongside Lavia rather than Malo Gusto, with Sports Mole the lone dissenter putting James at right wing-back instead. Second, Alonso's own framing of the Caicedo problem is more hopeful than Thursday's reporting suggested - his words were that hopefully it is not new and it was not more than last time - while Henderson is described as waiting on the green light for his debut after wrist surgery and Palestra still has no return date. Third, on the Arsenal side Mosquera's problem is now being reported specifically as a hamstring scare, with Ezri Konsa in line to start alongside Gabriel, and there is a genuine split over Arsenal's second midfielder: NBC Sports projects Myles Lewis-Skelly next to Declan Rice, while Yahoo Sport and Sports Mole expect Bruno Guimaraes to be fit enough to start. Christos Tzolis is expected on the left but Eberechi Eze is competition for that shirt. One forward-looking note worth having in front of you: Cole Palmer is one goal away from 50 Premier League goals for Chelsea, which he would reach inside 100 appearances - a club record pace. Odds, kickoff and channel were all re-verified on Friday evening and none of them moved: DraftKings still have Arsenal -155, the draw +260 and Chelsea +380, and it is 10:30am Central on USA Network with Telemundo carrying the Spanish call. SATURDAY 5 SEPTEMBER UPDATE (morning Central). The Caicedo decision has still not been made public, and by Alonso's own timetable it will not be until later today - the final session at Cobham is under way as this is written and the squad is picked off the back of it. So nothing has actually resolved overnight: he remains a genuine doubt rather than an absentee, and the XI projected here still assumes he does not start. If he is passed fit he starts, and the midfield reshapes around him in a way none of the published projections capture. Two things did move. First, the market: DraftKings now price Chelsea +370, in from +380 on Friday and +425 on Thursday, while Arsenal -155 and the draw +260 have now held through three straight checks. So the drift is consistently one-way and consistently small - Chelsea are being backed, but the de-vigged read is still only 20 percent Chelsea, 25 percent draw, 55 percent Arsenal, and Arsenal remain a clear favourite. Second, Arsenal's midfield question has largely resolved: Friday's split between Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes has tipped, and the previews checked this morning now converge on Guimaraes starting alongside Declan Rice. Cristhian Mosquera's hamstring scare has not cleared, so Ezri Konsa is expected in alongside Gabriel for his first competitive Arsenal start. The rest of the expected Arsenal shape is Raya in goal, White and Calafiori at full-back, and Saka, Odegaard and Christos Tzolis behind Kai Havertz, with Saliba and Timber both unavailable. Kickoff and channel were re-checked this morning and are unchanged for a third time: 16:30 UK, 10:30am Central, USA Network. One caution worth recording, because it nearly caused an error here: a prominent Sports Illustrated headline reading 'triple Chelsea fitness update for Arsenal tie as Caicedo ruled out' is a January 2026 article about an entirely different two-legged cup fixture under a different head coach, in which Caicedo was suspended rather than injured. It has nothing to do with Sunday and was discarded. That is the second stale-source trap on this fixture in two days.

lineupNote: This is a guess, and the honest headline is that the previewers have moved and this page has moved with them. Every serious preview published on Friday now has Reece James starting - they simply disagree about where. NBC Sports, Yahoo Sport and The Chelsea Chronicle all put him in the central pair alongside Romeo Lavia, and that is the version projected here, which pushes Malo Gusto out of the eleven Thursday's page had him in. Sports Mole instead keeps Gusto next to Lavia and starts James at right wing-back in place of Pedro Neto, on the reasoning that Alonso may want a more defensive profile on that flank at the Emirates. Either way the back three, the goalkeeper, the two tens and the striker are the same in all four versions, so the argument is confined to one flank and one midfield slot. Behind all of it sits Moises Caicedo. Alonso would not rule him out on Friday - his line on the problem was that hopefully it is not new and not worse than last time - and said the decision comes after Saturday's final session. If Caicedo is passed fit he starts, and the midfield question resolves itself in a way none of these projections capture. Jordan Henderson is still waiting on the green light for his Chelsea debut after wrist surgery, and Marco Palestra has no return date. Martinez keeps the goalkeeping job by default with Robert Sanchez on loan at Como. Malo Gusto, Valentin Barco, Josh Acheampong, Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck are the likeliest bench options. Treat all of this as provisional until the team sheet lands about an hour before kickoff. SATURDAY MORNING: no change to the eleven above, and still no word on Caicedo - his fitness test is happening today and the announcement should come with the squad, or failing that with the team sheet about an hour before kickoff. Treat the midfield as the one genuinely unsettled area of this projection.

notes: An all-Premier League tie at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's third home match in under three weeks. Leeds are managed by Daniel Farke and are back in the third round for the first time since 2022/23. Date and kick-off are confirmed by Chelsea: Wednesday 9 September, 8pm UK, which is 2pm Central. UK coverage is Sky Sports Main Event. For US viewers the important point is that this is NOT an NBC competition - CBS and Paramount Plus hold the American rights to the Carabao Cup, and Paramount Plus streams the large majority of ties in every round, which is also where the second-round tie was carried. The per-match US listing had still not been published as of 5 September, so treat the platform as reliable and a specific channel number as unconfirmed. No mainstream sportsbook had priced this tie as of 5 September either. The only numbers circulating are tipster model projections, which are not odds and are not recorded here, so the odds fields are deliberately still empty and will be filled once a real book posts a line - most likely once the Arsenal match is out of the way. There is also no basis yet for a projected XI: Alonso's pre-match press conference does not happen until early in the week. What can be said is that the tie falls three days after the Arsenal away trip and four days before Hull at home, and Alonso rotated heavily in the second round, so a much-changed side should be the expectation rather than a surprise.
